Phoebe was first introduced in the 1987 book, The Magic School Bus Inside the Earth. Carlos and Keesha were added in the 1994 book, The Magic School Bus In the Time of Dinosaurs.\nIn the other books and merchandise --including the TV series and TV tie-in books-- Ms. Frizzle's class was whittled down to eight kids (Arnold, Carlos, Dorothy Ann, Keesha, Phoebe, Ralphie, Tim and Wanda)."},{"level":"1","index":"3","type":"text","title":"List_of_books_and_merchandise","content":"Original series books\nNotes: *The Science Fair Expedition released 20 years after at its anniversary.\nChapter books\nScholastic Reader Level 2\nTV tie-in books\nTV tie-in fun kits\nA Science Fact Finder Book\nMs. Frizzle's Adventures\nLiz series\nMagic School Bus Presents: A Nonfiction Companion to the Original Magic School Bus Series\nDVDs\nVHS"},{"level":"1","index":"4","type":"text","title":"Individual_books","content":"The original Magic School Bus books are:\nThe Magic School Bus at the Waterworks (ISBN 0-590-40360-5, 1986)\nTheme: the water cycle and the waterworks\nMs Frizzle's class is going with her on the most boring field trip, to the waterworks. At least that is what they think until they discover how interesting things always happen on Ms Frizzle's trips. After going through a tunnel, all the children find themselves in scuba diving outfits. On the top of a bridge the bus rises up in the air and into a cloud. Once in the cloud, the class finds that water droplets are growing, and they are shrinking. The class rains and lands in the water purification system. Eventually it takes them back to Walkerville Elementary, where they come out of the faucet in the girls' bathroom. Later, they see the bus outside and wonder how it returned from the cloud.\nThe Magic School Bus Inside the Earth (ISBN 0-590-40760-0, 1987)\nTheme: geology\nMs Frizzle's class is starting a unit on geology and for homework every student has to find a rock, and bring it to school. The next day every child except Phil has an excuse, so Ms Frizzle decides to take the class on a field trip to collect rocks. The class starts digging until they, with the help of the magic bus, dig all the way through the center of Earth. They collect many rocks and learn about the different types. Phoebe Terese first appears in this book as the \"new kid\". Before the show was even in production, the Magic School Bus appeared on PBS, because this book was featured on Reading Rainbow.\nThe Magic School Bus Inside the Human Body (ISBN 0-590-41427-5, 1989)\nTheme: the human body\nMs Frizzle's class is going to the museum to see an exhibit on the human body. However they stop for lunch at a park and Arnold Perlstein takes too long to eat. When Ms Frizzle tries to hit the horn to tell him to hurry, she \"accidentally\" pushes a strange little button on the dashboard and the class finds itself inside a human body, but they are unaware that it is Arnold's. They go through the digestive system and brain and out through the nose.\nThe Magic School Bus Lost in the Solar System (ISBN 0-590-41429-1, 1990)\nTheme: the Solar System\nArnold's know-it-all cousin Janet, is coming on the field trip this time. They are going to the planetarium to see a show about the Solar System, but it is closed for repairs. On the way back to school, they blast off and fly into outer space. They visit all the planets and learn about them, but in the asteroid belt, they lose Ms Frizzle and find themselves lost in space. The rocket bus featured in this book has become a symbol of the Magic School Bus series.\nThe Magic School Bus On the Ocean Floor (ISBN 0-590-41431-3, 1992)\nTheme: the ocean\nMs Frizzle's class is learning about the ocean. It is really hot and the children just want a break. They are thrilled when she says they will take a trip to the ocean. When she gets to the beach she starts to drive into the water and they realise that when Ms Frizzle says \"ocean\" she means \"ocean\". Believing the bus is in trouble, Lenny the Lifeguard decides to try to save the children and instead finds himself accompanying them on the field trip.\nThe Magic School Bus In the Time of the Dinosaurs (ISBN 0-590-44689-4, 1994)\nTheme: dinosaurs\nThe children are turning their classroom into Dinosaur Land for Parents' Night, as they are studying dinosaurs. Ms. Frizzle receives a letter from an old high school friend who is now a paleontologist and she decides to take the class on a trip to the dig. When she discovers that they are missing the bones of some Maiasaurs, she turns the bus into a time machine to travel back to the age of dinosaurs to find the bones. The class sees dinosaurs and learns the name of the different periods of the era and other information. This is the first time Ms Frizzle's first name is mentioned, and it is the first appearance of Carlos Ramon and Keesha Franklin, although Keesha was first seen in The Magic School Bus: On the Ocean Floor.\nThe Magic School Bus Inside a Hurricane (ISBN 0-590-44687-8, 1995)\nTheme: weather\nThe class is going to the weather station to learn about weather. However, on the way there the bus turns into a hot air balloon. Eventually they find themselves inside a hurricane. Ms Frizzle's radio proves an annoyance to Arnold in this book, as it seems to know his name.\nThe Magic School Bus Inside a Beehive (1996)\nTheme: bees\nThe class is now learning about insects and Ms Frizzle is taking her class on a trip to meet a beekeeper, but they beat the beekeeper there. While they are waiting, Ms Frizzle accidentally pushes a small lever which turns the bus into a tiny beehive and the class (including Ms Frizzle) into bees. They explore the hive and learn about bees, but can they save the hive from a bear?\nThe Magic School Bus and the Electric Field Trip (1998)\nTheme: electricity\nThe children in Ms Frizzle's class were sure that there was nobody like her, but that was before they met her niece, Dottie Frizzle. Dottie accompanies the class on their field trip to the town power plant. There the bus turns into a dump truck, and pours the children into the plant. They shrink and travel through the Walkerville electric system.\nThe Magic School Bus Explores the Senses (1999)\nTheme: the five senses\nThe class is learning about the senses and they are going to sing a song for an important teacher meeting. However, Ms Frizzle's personality and clothes make the class forget. Ms Frizzle thinks the meeting is tomorrow, but it is really today. So Mr. Wilde, the assistant principal, decides to catch her so he can tell her about the meeting. He decides to get in a bus that just happens to be the magic school bus. The class decides to accompany him. They cannot let him drive that bus, not all by himself. Mr. Wilde accidentally shrinks the bus and soon he and the class find themselves on a trip exploring the senses. Mr. Wilde soon becomes obsessed with driving the bus and forgets all about finding Ms Frizzle, but the class does not. Ms Frizzle's mother appears in this book.\nThe Magic School Bus and the Science Fair Expedition (ISBN 0-590-10824-7; 2006)\nTheme: famous scientists in history\nThe first MSB book since 1999, The Magic School Bus celebrated its 20th anniversary with this new book published on 1 August 2006. Ms. Frizzle and her class have to find projects to display at the Walkerville Science Fair, and fast. They decide to consult with famous scientists in history like Louis Pasteur, George Washington Carver, Charles Darwin, Marie Curie, Isaac Newton, Galileo Galilei, even Albert Einstein. All the original characters are in this book.\nThe Magic School Bus and the Climate Challenge (ISBN 0-590-10826-3; 2010)\nTheme: climate change\nMs. Frizzle takes the class on a flight on the bus over the arctic, showing them how the polar ice caps have melted since Ms. Frizzle's old copy of Our Wonderful World was published. They travel around the earth, observing the impacts of global warming and alternative energy sources. FAQ

What genre are The Magic School Bus books?

The books are a combination of fiction and nonfiction. The frame story of the bus and its passengers is fictional, while the scientific facts in the books are true.

What grade level are The Magic School Bus books?

The books in the original series are recommended for children who read at grade levels 1-3. The chapter books are written for older children who read at grade levels 2-5.

How many books are in The Magic School Bus series?

The original series of books is comprised of thirteen books. There are also a number of chapter books, videos, and web adaptations of The Magic School Bus series.

The Magic School Bus by Joanna Cole

The Magic School Bus by Joanna Cole is a series of books published by Scholastic. When Scholastic editorial director Craig Walker noticed that teachers were frequently requesting science books from the publisher, he thought that books that combined science with humor might be an engaging way to approach the topic of science for young readers. The books are fictional, although they present scientific information to readers within a fictional setting.

Walker was aware of Cole's first book and thought she would be a good fit for the task. Titled Cockroaches, Cole's 1971 book combined science and humor. Walker asked her, along with illustrator Bruce Degen, to work on the project.

The Magic School Bus book series is about a science teacher who guides her students on field trips aboard an old school bus. This frame story, which is a narrative device used to frame or surround another story, appears throughout the original series. When the teacher and her students arrive at their destination, they explore a scientific topic such as the human body, insects, or even space. The books are set in the present day, but since the bus is magic, it is capable of time travel. The series uses the teacher and students to engage readers in scientific topics.

The Magic School Bus books have won many awards, including the NEA Foundation Award for Outstanding Service to Public Education, the Oppenheim Toy Portfolio Gold Award Parents' Choice Award. In addition the books have been named the American Booksellers Association Choice, the IRA/CBC Children's Choice, the School Library Journal Best Books of the Year, the NCTE Notable Children's Book in the Language Arts, the IRA Teachers' Choice, the Horn Book Fanfare, the Parent's Magazine Best Books of the Year, and the Reading Rainbow Selection.

The Magic School Bus book series was published by Scholastic. Joanna Cole authored the original series, but several other writers were involved in creating the later chapter books based on the series. Cole's favorite subject in school was science, and she also enjoyed writing reports on science topics. The Magic School Bus is fictional, but its focus is on scientific concepts. Additional Info

What is the Magic School Bus?

The Magic School Bus is a bus that can transform into things, fly, shrink, and go back in time just to name a few. It can travel inside bodies, to outer space, or inside a hurricane! Doesn't that sound like it would make for some amazing school field trips?

However, the Magic School Bus isn't real; it is part of a series of fictional (made up) books about science written by Joanna Cole. This means that the events are made up, but the books discuss and teach you about real scientific facts!

In the book series, the children in Ms. Frizzle's class and their class pet, Liz the lizard, get to go on cool field trips whenever they discuss a science topic. They learn about it on the field trip, and when they come back to school, they are able to discuss or apply it to their lesson or life. At the end of each book, there is also a page discussing the scientific facts the reader learned about in the book.

In The Magic School Bus book series, the students take field trips on a bus like this one.

About the Author

Joanna Cole was born in 1944 in New Jersey. When she was in school, science was her favorite subject. She also had a teacher like Ms. Frizzle, who she probably used as a model for her books. Joanna was able to use her love of science to figure out a perfect career--writing about science!

When Joanna writes a book, she has to do lots and lots of research. She has to read all about her topic, visit any museums or places that will give her more information, and speak to people who know lots about the subject. She also mixes jokes into all of her books because she loves humor as much as she loves science.

Joanna has written over 90 books, with 'The Magic School Bus' series being her most popular. It has even been turned into a TV show and made into movies!

Popular Books in the Series

'The Magic School Bus' series started out with 12 original books. It then expanded into chapter books, books that go along with the TV series, nonfiction books, and books about Ms. Frizzle's adventures. 《新概念英语》经典版和青少版的区别

2017-08-03 11:06

来源：新东方在线

作者：

《新概念英语》经典版和青少版的区别由长春新东方同步新东方在线整理发布，更多精彩内容，请持续关注长春新东方官方网站及长春新东方学校公众号【ccxdfcn】。

说到《新概念英语》，相信大部分都知道是指下面的这套外研社出版的教材(共4册)：


上面这套教材一般被叫作成人版或经典版新概念。这是因为不少人可能还不知道，其实外研社还出版了一套青少版的《新概念英语》，就是下面这套(共6个级别，入门级到5A5B)：

一、《新概念英语》经典版

《新概念英语》经典版(New Concept English)，恐怕是迄今为止在中国大陆地区甚至是全世界使用时间最长的英语学习教材。作者路易斯·乔治·亚历山大(L. G. Alexander)是英语交际法教学的代表人物。

本套教材由朗文公司(Longman group)最早出版于1967年，1993年发行了修订版。中国现在出版的该教材授权版本是外语教学与研究出版社和朗文出版亚洲有限公司联合出版的1997年版本，配套录音是英音，由北京外语音像出版社出版(该出版社2006年又出版了美音版录音带)。

本套教材共分四册，大致内容如下：

第一册：英语初阶(First Things First)

该册的课文都是以对话的形式为主来编写的，侧重的是生活常见场景的语言运用能力的培养。全册共分为144课时，其中单课基本都是对话形式的课文，而双课则是以练习为主的单课内容的巩固和提高。

第二册：实践与进步(Practice & Progress)

从该册开始，课文都是篇章形式。本册共96课，分为四个单元，其中第四单元是为了衔接第二册与第三册而设立，所以难度较大。新概念英语的第二册被许多人认为是一部经典的教材，而它同时也是整部教材中最关键的一册，国内的英语学习者基本都认为只要学好了第二册，要通过诸如中考、高考、大学英语四六级甚至是考研英语等水平测试问题就不大了。事实也是如此，只是大部分学习者都是学完了第二册，但并没有学好。

第三册：培养技能(Developing Skills)

该册共60课，分为三个单元。本册属中级水平的综合教材，着重分析句子之间内在的逻辑关系，让学员充分认识和领悟英文句型的实用性，从而运用到生活实际当中;同时，将进一步扩充讲解词汇、语法及句型的实战运用。

第四册：流利英语(Fluency in English)

该册1997年版的共48课，分为6个单元。新概念教材最精华的一册，也是最有难度的一册。学习者通过在前三册的学习，已经为自己打下了一定坚实的英语基础，而第四册覆盖了一些具有科学的专业学术文章，学习者将会更好的提高自己对英美文化以及一些专业肤浅知识(原版)的了解。

二、《新概念英语》青少版

《新概念英语青少版》(Junior New Concept English)是由外研社于2008年引进出版的，其前身为由亚历山大生前主编的绝笔之作——Target。Target是由朗文公司于1973年出版的，共分为三个级别。外研社引入之后，Target的三个级别分别对应的是《新概念英语青少版》的1A1B、2A2B、3A3B。

外研社又在这三个级别的基础上，往前增加了入门级，分为A、B两个分册;往后又增加了4A4B和5A5B两个级别。


三、《新概念英语》经典版和青少版的异同

《新概念英语青少版》入门级并非零起点，但是从26个字母的学习开始的;1A1B、2A2B、3A3B的知识点与《新概念英语》经典版第一册的知识点基本对应;4A4B和5A5B的知识点与新概念英语》经典版第二册的知识点基本对应。

此外，《新概念英语青少版》相比于《新概念英语》经典版，具有以下特点：

1、对话与课文是以一个英国家庭以及他们的朋友的故事为主线的;

Think British English

Think Second edition is the English course that develops your students as learners and encourages them to think big – in English.

Have you ever wondered what the world will be like in 50 years’ time™ Or thought about the impact of social media and how it affects you™ Think Second edition is the English course that develops your students as learners and challenges them to consider global issues such as climate change and important scientific discoveries. With inspirational topics and texts from around the world, pages dedicated to Life Competencies and focused practice for Cambridge English Qualifications, this course encourages students to think big – in English.

Authors

Herbert Puchta, Jeff Stranks, Peter Lewis-Jones

CEFR level:
A1 - C1
Components:
32
Published:
November 2019
Edition:
2nd Edition

Key features

Develop students’ vital skills for the future, all mapped to the Cambridge Framework for Life Competencies.

Test & Train in Levels 1, 2, 4 and 5 provides perfect on-the-go preparation for Cambridge English Qualifications across all devices.

Build students’ confidence for Cambridge English Qualifications with exam practice checked by Assessment experts in Cambridge.

Give language a context with entertaining vlogs, grammar animations and documentary videos throughout.

Challenge and inspire your students with thought-provoking global topics like climate change and what is fake news.

The Digital Pack on Cambridge One includes Presentation Plus, Practice Extra, Collaboration Plus, interactive eBooks, tests and more.

What makes Think 2nd Edition special?

How to find out more

Request free sample

Get an e-sample that will allow you to view a product preview on your desktop.

Free sample
Meet the authors

Herbert Puchta

Herbert Puchta holds a PhD in ELT Pedagogy, was Professor of English at the Teacher Training University in Graz, Austria, and is a well-known plenary speaker at numerous international conferences. He was also President of IATEFL, the International Association of Teachers of English as a Foreign Language.

For more than three decades, Herbert has done research into the practical application of findings from cognitive psychology and brain research to the teaching of English as a foreign language. Herbert has written numerous course books as well as articles and resource books.

His latest resource books are Activities for Very Young Learners and 101 Tips for Teaching Teenagers. His most recent course books are Super Minds 2nd edition for primary students, Think 2nd edition for teens, and Empower 2nd edition for adults and young adults, all published by Cambridge University Press.

Jeff Stranks

Jeff Stranks has worked in ELT for more than four decades, as a teacher, teacher trainer and now materials writer. He is a co-author of titles such as English in Mind, Think, Citizen Z and Empower with Cambridge University Press, and has also published in other countries. He has been based in Brazil since 1991, and now lives in Brasilia.

Peter Lewis-Jones

Peter Lewis-Jones is a freelance author who has been involved in EFL since 1993. After stints abroad teaching in Italy, Egypt, Indonesia and Brazil, he returned to the UK in 2006 to concentrate on writing. He now lives on the North Wales border with his family. In his spare time, he can be found bird watching somewhere on the Wirral.

He is co-author on a number of Cambridge EFL titles including English in Mind, MORE!, Super Minds and Think.

Thinking beyond language

Think 2nd edition offers a holistic approach to learning, giving students not only the language, but also the skills they need for future success beyond the classroom.

The reading texts, writing, and listening scripts are carefully chosen to reflect teenage interests, with inspiring and thought-provoking topics throughout, including music, films, TV and important global issues. For accessibility, all texts are also available in audio format. Students are challenged by topics like eating bugs, teenage inventors, digital detoxes and fake news.

Think Values encourage students to reflect on and discuss a wide range of important values, helping to develop their character as well as their sensitivity to others.

Train to Think sections and Me and My World features encourage students to reflect on the topics presented and to express their opinions on meaningful issues, as well as requiring them to work together to achieve consensus or to solve a problem.

Culture sections introduce interesting topics and information about people and places around the world, sparking discussion that requires students to make use of the information presented.

Support for mixed abilities

Think 2nd edition includes extensive support for teachers with mixed-ability classes, including graded Workbook activities, extra ideas and extension activities in the Teacher's Book, and additional content in the Resource Bank.

Get it Right! activities help students avoid common errors, as identified in the Cambridge English Learner Corpus.

Relatable and motivating videos

Over 30 new videos including documentaries, vlogs and grammar videos, grab students’ attention and give language a context.

Documentaries

Every unit is launched with a documentary style video, exploring global issues and topics to pique student’s curiosity in the world around them and get them thinking critically.

Grammar videos

Short, catchy animated grammar raps in the early levels and grammar videos in levels 4 and 5 explain grammar concepts in a fun and memorable way.

Vlogs

The Cambridge Life Competencies are embodied in entertaining vlogs recorded by students.

Digital tools

The Think 2nd edition digital package on Cambridge One

 • Plan: all your teaching materials, all in one place.
 • Present: interactive Student's Book and Workbook with embedded audio and video.
 • Practise: mobile-friendly bite-sized practice activities and games for every unit of the Student's Book.
 • Collaborate: students can collaborate on project work remotely.
 • Motivate: medals for completing activities provide motivation to do extra practice.
 • Assess: see student performance at a glance and download ready-made tests.

Presentation Plus

 • Student’s Book and Workbook with interactive exercises.
 • Embedded links to classroom audio and video.
 • Extra class activities and games.
 • Accessible online and offline.

Practice Extra

 • Mobile friendly platform and content.
 • Bite-sized learning activities with audio and video.
 • Online speaking tasks.
 • Performance tracking.

Collaboration Plus

Students can work together remotely in the collaboration space, where teachers can set, track and assess their work. Teachers can also share students' project work with the class in the Showcase area.

Teacher's Resource Bank

Online teacher resource area with support for projects, graded grammar and vocabulary practice worksheets, video worksheets, writing templates, extra speaking activities and more!

Test & Train

On-the-go and intuitive - the perfect training tool for Cambridge English Qualifications. Exam practice and timed practice tests get students ready for exam day.

Test Generator

Create your own tests as and when you require them. An easy-to-use tool to customise and create end of unit/end of term/end of year tests as well as exam practice tests. Provides opportunities for revising and testing what students have learned.

Digital Pack contents

 • Student's Pack includes access to Interactive eBook and eWorkbook, Practice Extra, Collaboration Plus, Learner Resources and Test & Train.
 • Teacher's Pack includes access to audio and video files, Presentation Plus (includes interactive eBooks), Practice Extra, Collaboration Plus, Test Generator, Test & Train and Teacher’s Resources.

To access theThink 2nd edition digital materials, go to cambridgeone.org
Life Competencies

How can we prepare our students to succeed in a world that is rapidly changing? We need to help our students with the skills and experiences that go beyond simply learning an additional language.

We work closely with educators to understand how these skills – Cambridge Life Competencies – can integrate seamlessly into your English language programme.

Dedicated Life Competencies pages in Think 2nd edition include entertaining ‘life lessons’ vlogs recorded by students, with each focusing on developing a key competency area from the Cambridge Life Competencies Framework. Students also have the opportunity to reflect on the themes and topics in the new Me and My World feature.

Find out more
Exam content

Focused Exams sections in Think 2nd edition cover A2 Key for Schools, B1 Preliminary for Schools, B2 First for Schools and C1 Advanced.

Clearly labelled and updated exam exercises in every other unit replicate the format of the exams and build students’ confidence, with exam content checked by Cambridge Assessment English for accuracy and level.

Test Yourself pages allow students to check their progress and are based on the language presented in the previous pair of units.

The Workbook also offers extra practice and useful tips for students in Cambridge Exams Practice sections.

Test & Train offers additional test practice experience with the added bonus of a timed Practice Test and is available across digital devices.
